span.label: mechanisms
span.term: Because the hippocampus alone integrates successive events together with the context in which they occurred, it can build context-specific branching representations, which is why the developing temporal linkage appears there and not in amygdala or cingulate cortex
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: mechanisms
span.term: Memory formation is the internal convergence of one network state onto the network state representing the stimulus that followed it in time, so that each state comes to lead reliably to the next
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: mutual information between successive time bins measures how much knowing activity now reduces uncertainty about activity next, which linear correlation cannot capture
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: the analysis deliberately avoids assuming a constant representation, looking at a neuron's relation to itself over time rather than to the stimulus
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: the increase comes from reduced conditional entropy rather than raised marginal entropy, so it is the relationship changing and not the firing statistics
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: the hippocampus is proposed to be the site because it alone can integrate successive events with the context in which they occurred, allowing branching representations

span.label: memories are framed as stable network states, with formation meaning one state leads more reliably to the next
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: With repeated viewing of the same clip, firing in one 250-ms window became increasingly informative about firing in the next window, so earlier activity came to predict later activity.
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: This linkage appeared after only two or three viewings of an episode and was stronger than both context-independent and stimulus-driven correlations.
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: The gradual growth of temporal relationships across clip repetitions occurred in the hippocampus only, not in amygdala, anterior cingulate or entorhinal cortex at the single-cell level.
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: The strength of hippocampal temporal relationships during viewing predicted how many clips a subject later recalled freely, with a correlation of 0.87 across subjects.
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: The effect was not an artifact of changing firing rates, because mean firing rate was stable across both clip repetition and clip duration.
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: Decomposing mutual information showed the rise came from falling conditional entropy (better prediction of the next window) rather than from rising marginal entropy (changed firing statistics).
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: When pairs and triplets of simultaneously recorded cells were analysed, the increase in temporal relationships appeared in entorhinal cortex as well as hippocampus, but still not in amygdala or anterior cingulate.
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.
